Stop calling an asynchronous function that keeps failing

Source: R/async_circuit_breaker.R
async_circuit_breaker.Rd

Asynchronous version of circuit_breaker(), for functions that return a promise. It has the same states and arguments. A call fails when its promise rejects, or the function throws. Once the circuit is open, calls return a promise already rejected with fnware_circuit_open, without running the function.

Usage

async_circuit_breaker(f, failures = 5, reset_after = 30)

Arguments

f

The function to decorate. Usually supplied by %@% rather than directly.

failures

Number of consecutive errors that open the circuit. A whole number of at least 1. Defaults to 5.

reset_after

Seconds the circuit stays open before a trial call. A number greater than 0. Defaults to 30.

Value

A decorator. The decorated function returns a promise.

Details

Calls overlap, so a failure is counted when its promise rejects, and calls made before earlier ones settle all go through. Two more rules:

  • While half-open, only one trial call runs and others are rejected. A trial not settled after reset_after seconds is abandoned, so a promise that never settles cannot hold the circuit shut. Put async_timeout() inside to bound it sooner.

  • A call that started before the circuit opened cannot close it, or be counted again, when it settles.

Stack it outside async_retry(). Needs the promises package and an event loop.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
down <- function() promises::promise_reject(simpleError("service down"))
f := async_circuit_breaker(failures = 2, reset_after = 60) %@% down

# Failures are counted when a promise settles, so let each call settle
try_once <- function() {
  promises::then(f(), onRejected = function(err) cat(class(err)[[1]], "\n"))
  while (!later::loop_empty()) later::run_now(0.1)
}
try_once() # simpleError
try_once() # simpleError, and the circuit opens
try_once() # fnware_circuit_open, down() was not called

fetch := async_circuit_breaker(failures = 3, reset_after = 30) %@%
  async_retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(3)) %@%
  function(url) down()
} # }
